title: Handoff + Latency Deep Dive — Week of 2027-03-15
content:
Purpose:
This is the working note for the SRE weekly sync covering the on-call handoff for Mar 15–21, a short incident summary from last week, current SLO health, and an actionable plan for the latency micro-batching experiment we want to run next week. Treat as living doc — add observations, logs, and quick experiment outputs here.

Attendees (async + live):
- Asha Patel (owner)
- Connor Liu (on-call)
- Marta Gomez (serving-runtime)
- Ethan Park (platform infra)
- Priya R. (observability — recorded notes)

Quick TL;DR:
- Incident on Mar 11 (INC-2027-03-11) caused elevated p50/p95 for hosted-api in us-west; root cause: uneven KV cache eviction after a config rollout. No customer data exposed; elevated error budget consumption for a few routes.
- Current service-level snapshot (see SLO section) shows 99.92% availability vs target 99.95% for hosted-api; error budget remaining 0.45% for the month.
- Action: short term fixes merged; longer-term mitigation: add per-route cache warmup and eviction backoff, plus an observability alert for sudden K/V churn.
- Next big block: run latency micro-batching experiment to evaluate batching window vs tail-latency on P4/Trn-config.

Incident summary (INC-2027-03-11):
- Impact: increased token latency and occasional 5xx on dedicated routing for 14 minutes (Mar 11 02:12–02:26 UTC).
- User impact: some realtime chat sessions saw stalls; no data loss. Estimated affected requests: ~12k requests (0.02% of daily volume).
- Detection: anomaly alert from p95-alarm (Grafana) followed by on-call Slack bridge.
- Root cause hypothesis: config rollout (PR #1782) toggled a new eviction heuristic. Under a specific seq-len distribution, the heuristic aggressively evicted large prefix caches, causing higher recompute and KV churn.
- Mitigation: rolled back the heuristic flag at 02:20 UTC (manual rollback by Connor). Autoscaler back-filled capacity; traffic normalized by 02:26.
- Postmortem action items (see tasks below).

SLO snapshot (as of Mar 15 07:00 UTC):
- hosted-api availability (global): 99.92% (30d window) — target 99.95%
- dedicated-p99-latency (seq<=1024): 210ms (current) — SLO p99 <= 200ms
- embeddings-service error-rate: 0.03% — SLO <= 0.1% (good)
- Notes: availability slack mostly consumed in us-west after incident; teams should prioritize reducing p99 latency on seq<=1024 path.

Open/runbook gaps discovered:
- No runbook step for "cache churn detection" — the view we had was per-host memory, not per-model KV eviction rate. Need a simple signal (per-model eviction rate > X in Y min).
- Canary rollouts don't automatically disable heuristics on degraded latency — add an automatic rollback guard in rollout-controller.

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Asha: Draft runbook entry for cache-churn detection and alert thresholds (ETA: 2027-03-18).
- Connor: Add a Grafana panel for per-model KV eviction rate and add to critical dashboard (ETA: 2027-03-17). Linked ticket: JIRA-SRE-3421.
- Marta: Implement per-route eviction backoff logic in runtime (spike PR expected; ETA: 2027-03-29).
- Ethan: Add rollback guard to rollout-controller (playbook + PR review) (ETA: 2027-03-25).
- Priya: Synthetic traffic test that reproduces the seq-len distribution that triggered the incident (ETA: 2027-03-20).

Latency micro-batching experiment — plan overview:
- Goal: quantify tradeoff between batching window (ms) and p99 tail latency for seq<=1024 on P4-backed dedicated nodes. Particularly measure how small batch windows hurt throughput vs reduce serialization latency.
- Hypothesis: increasing batching window to 8–12ms will reduce per-token GPU time by ~12% at peak throughput but may increase p99 by <5ms for 95% of routes; for some low-QPS routes batching adds jitter.
- Test harness: use load-test harness under /tools/loadtest/micro-batch (wip). Test matrix: window = [0ms, 4ms, 8ms, 12ms], batch-size cap = [16, 32], concurrency = [50, 200].
- Metrics to capture: p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput (tokens/sec), GPU-utilization, KV-eviction-rate, request 5xx rate.
- Rollout plan: run synthetic tests in staging, canary on 5% traffic (dedicated), monitor p99 and error budget; abort if p99 increases >10% or 5xx >0.1% above baseline.
- Observability: add temporary alert rules scoped to canary tag. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/latency/serving-runtime-overview (add micro-batch panel).

On-call handoff checklist (to be included each handoff):
- Current on-call: Connor Liu; Next on-call: Ying Tan (starting 2027-03-17).
- Active incidents: INC-2027-03-11 (postmortem in progress).
- SLOs at-risk: hosted-api availability (listed above).
- Ongoing experiments: micro-batching (in planning); do not run without notifying on-call.
- Runbook quick links: runtime-cache-eviction, rollout-controller-guard, incident-template (Confluence links in linked_artifacts).
- Pager escalation path: pager -> on-call -> SRE lead -> eng manager (numbers in PagerDuty).

Meeting notes / decisions made live:
- We agreed to prioritize the cache-backoff change over micro-batching if the implementation conflicts with production safety (Marta/Ethan).
- Connor will add a short script that can detect elevated KV churn and temporarily disable the heuristic flag until rollback completes. That script will be run manually first, then automated (Connor, ETA 2027-03-18).
- Priya to run synthetic reproduction on Friday and drop the traffic qps/sample traces in this doc.

Logs & quick evidence (past 48h):
- Sample alert timeline: 02:12 UTC p95 spike -> 02:13 elevated eviction rate (host-23) -> 02:16 CPU/GPU pressure on dedicated pool -> 02:20 manual flag rollback -> 02:26 metrics normalize.
- Investigative notes: eviction spike correlated with a single model rollout that increased sequence-length-heavy traffic (model-id: rwd-llm-v2-large).

Postmortem checklist (short):
- Draft written (Asha) — link to postmortem page added to linked_artifacts.
- Customer notification: none required (internal-only impact).
- Follow-ups scheduled in JIRA (SRE-3421, SRE-3422 for runbook and rollback guard).

Quick wins (low effort):
- Add per-model eviction rate to existing runtime-metrics (Connor — 1 day).
- Add a temporary alert (eviction-rate > 100/min for 5 min) to staging only (Priya — 1 day).

Blockers / Risks:
- Platform calendar: any platform cluster maintenance next week may interfere with micro-batching tests — coordinate with infra (Ethan).
- Observability retention: fine-grained per-model metrics increase cardinality; SRE/observability should agree on sampling strategy.

Appendix: snippets + commands to run (for on-call)
- Check per-model eviction: grafana panel or metric query: sum(rate(kv_evictions_total{model="<model-id>"}[5m])) by (model)
- Rollback flag path: /api/admin/flags/runtime_eviction_heuristic -> set false (requires admin token).
- Run synthetic scenario: tools/loadtest/micro-batch --model rwd-llm-v2-large --seq-dist heavy-tail --qps 600 --duration 10m

Notes to self (raw):
- Keep experiment small, run staging first. If stash shows any 5xx spike, stop.
- Remember to update the on-call cheat sheet with the new grafana links.

If you add anything to this doc, prefix with initials and timestamp.
